preamble: Excrescence of [d]: a transitional voiced stop arises between a nasal or /l/ and a following liquid (/nr/ > /ndr/, /nl/ > /ndl/, /lr/ > /ldr/). The velum closes before the tongue releases, so a brief oral stop forms. It appears independently in English, Gallo-Romance and Catalan.

examples.note: Excrescent d between n and r (compare Dutch donder).
d inserted in the nl cluster.
After the post-tonic vowel was lost, the new n'r cluster got an excrescent d.
Wiktionary explicitly gives tendre as an epenthetic form of older tenre.
